Using dishwater to water plants is not universally endorsed. Some sources advise that dishwater can be used if the detergent lacks boron, bleach, or sodium and is applied carefully to avoid pests or root issues [d1,d5], while others report personal success reusing dishwater on ornamentals and fruit trees [d2,d3,d4]. In contrast, Pennsylvania’s public health guidance explicitly prohibits using dishwater for plants [d6], and additional warnings note potential contamination and nutrient uptake interference [d9]. Practical tips to save dishwater for garden use are also offered [d7,d8].
